channel.title: AI - Ars Technica
channel.description: Serving the Technologist since 1998. News, reviews, and analysis.

item.title: Trump admin tries to block Clean Air Act lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines
item.description: NAACP lawsuit says xAI uses gas turbines without permits for Grok data center.

item.title: Anthropic "pauses" token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK
item.description: Move originally planned for Monday would have heavily increased power users' costs.

item.title: Pentagon boasts of using AI to write reports mandated by Congress
item.description: Pentagon also claims 1.5 million personnel are using generative AI tools.

item.title: SpaceX to acquire AI coding platform Cursor for $60 billion
item.description: Separately, neither could compete. Now they hope they can.

item.title: Leaked financial docs show OpenAI is losing billions of dollars a year
item.description: Audited accounting shows growing revenues being dwarfed by R&D, other expenses.

item.title: Critical Copilot vulnerability allowed hackers to steal 2FA code from users
item.description: SearchLeak exploit shows why the industry's approach to LLM security fails over and over.

item.title: Chipmaker Nvidia seeks to raise over $25B in first bond deal since 2021
item.description: Debt sale set to test investor appetite for further exposure to AI sector amid a deluge of borrowing.

item.title: Anthropic shuts down Fable, Mythos models following Trump admin directive
item.description: Commerce dept. worries that a Fable 5 "jailbreak" could be a national security threat.

item.title: SpaceX is now a public company valued for its AI potential, so what comes next?
item.description: As of today, SpaceX is owned by investors who will want to see it make money.

item.title: Here's what Jeff Bezos' new startup Prometheus will do
item.description: It isn't the only startup tackling physical AI, but it's one of the best-funded.

item.title: Ukraine's one-time test used fully autonomous drones to kill Russian soldiers
item.description: Full autonomy is rare, but Ukraine is installing AI modules on drones and robots.

item.title: $130 billion in data center projects blocked by protests so far this year
item.description: Winning fight against AI data centers gives people a "taste of political power."

item.title: When it comes to total water use, AI data centers are a drop in the bucket
item.description: Even moderately sized data centers can have an outsized local impact.

item.title: Google sues Chinese cybercrime network that used Gemini to automate scams
item.description: The fraudsters allegedly targeted hundreds of thousands of people with Gemini-coded scams sites.

item.title: Pokémon Go players unwittingly contributed to tech with military drone uses
item.description: The repurposing of Pokémon Go data for AI training continues to draw scrutiny.

item.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a model that runs local AI 4x faster
item.description: Diffusion AI is most common in image generation, but it can make text outputs much faster.

item.title: Nobody needs AI to search the Internet, court says in ruling against Google
item.description: Google AI Overview court loss in Germany could spell doom for AI search industry.

item.title: Anthropic says these topics are too dangerous to let its Fable 5 model talk about
item.description: New frontier model refuses cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry queries.

item.title: Google announces Gemini 3.5 Live Translate for instant voice-to-voice translation
item.description: Voice translations preserve speaker's tone, pacing, pitch—with SynthID watermarks for security.

item.title: Apple says its AI is still private, even when it's running on Google's servers
item.description: Some models run in Google's cloud, but without giving Google any kind of access.
